value.answer: For most adults, short-term use is considered safe. Side effects are usually mild: headaches, dizziness, nausea, sleepiness, stomachache, sometimes vivid dreams. Long-term safety isn't well studied. A preliminary study presented in November 2025 linked long-term use in people with chronic insomnia to a higher chance of heart failure, but it doesn't prove melatonin caused it, and it hasn't been peer-reviewed. Doses above 2 to 3 mg usually don't work better and just add side effects. Talk to a doctor first if you take blood thinners or immunosuppressants, are pregnant or trying to conceive, or want to take it every night for more than a few weeks. Don't combine it with benzodiazepines or zolpidem without medical advice, since the sedation can add up. Supplement quality also varies a lot, with some products containing much more or less than the label says.
